offense_class: Misdemeanor (1st–2nd offense); Gross Misdemeanor (3rd offense within 10 years or aggravated); Felony (4th offense or more within 10 years)
elements: Defendant drove, operated, or was in physical control of a motor vehicle
While under the influence of alcohol, a controlled substance, an intoxicating substance, or any combination
Defendant's ability to drive was impaired OR had an alcohol concentration of 0.08 or more
mandatory_minimum: None for first offense; 30 days (or 48 hours if aggravating factor) for second offense; 90 days for third; 180 days for felony DWI
enhancements: Alcohol concentration of 0.16 or more (aggravating factor)
Prior qualified impaired driving incident within 10 years
Refusal to submit to chemical test (gross misdemeanor or felony)
notes: Minnesota uses a 'look-back' period of 10 years for prior qualifying offenses. Implied consent law at § 169A.51. License plate impoundment and vehicle forfeiture possible.

elements: Defendant drove, operated, or was in physical control of a motor vehicle
While under the influence of alcohol or a controlled substance
Ability impaired OR alcohol concentration of 0.08 or more
No prior qualified impaired driving incidents within 10 years
enhancements: Alcohol concentration 0.16+ elevates to third-degree (gross misdemeanor)
notes: Fourth-degree DWI per § 169A.27. Driver's license revocation for 90 days minimum.

elements: Defendant drove, operated, or was in physical control of a motor vehicle
While under the influence of alcohol or controlled substance
Two or more aggravating factors present within 10 years
notes: Aggravating factors defined at § 169A.03, subd. 3. Two or more factors elevate from third to second degree.

elements: Defendant drove, operated, or was in physical control of a motor vehicle
While impaired by alcohol or controlled substance
Defendant has three or more qualified prior impaired driving incidents within 10 years, OR has a prior felony DWI conviction
mandatory_minimum: 180 days (may serve on electronic monitoring after 60 days)
notes: Lifetime lookback for prior felony DWI convictions. Vehicle forfeiture mandatory.

offense_class: Misdemeanor (first); escalates same as alcohol DWI
elements: Defendant drove, operated, or was in physical control of a motor vehicle
While under the influence of a controlled substance as defined in Chapter 152
Defendant's ability to drive was impaired by the substance
enhancements: Same aggravating factor framework as alcohol DWI
Combination of alcohol and controlled substances
notes: Includes Schedule I through V substances. Drug recognition evaluator (DRE) testimony commonly used. No per se limit for drugs — impairment must be proven.

penalty_max: 10 years (death); 5 years (great bodily harm); 3 years (substantial bodily harm)
elements: Defendant operated a motor vehicle
In a grossly negligent manner, while under the influence of alcohol or controlled substance, or in a negligent manner while impaired
Operation resulted in the death of or great bodily harm to another
notes: Separate offense from DWI — may be charged concurrently. Includes operation with any amount of Schedule I or II substance (except marijuana).

statute_title: Controlled Substance Crime in the Fifth Degree
elements: Defendant unlawfully possessed one or more mixtures containing a controlled substance classified in Schedule I, II, III, or IV
Possession was without a valid prescription
enhancements: Possession in a school zone, park, or public housing zone
notes: Lowest felony-level drug possession. First-time offenders often eligible for stay of adjudication or diversion. Minnesota has five degrees of controlled substance crimes.

statute_title: Possession of a Small Amount of Marijuana
elements: Defendant possessed a small amount of marijuana
Marijuana was not in a motor vehicle (motor vehicle elevates penalty)
enhancements: Sale of a small amount without remuneration
notes: Minnesota legalized adult-use cannabis effective 2023. Possession limits for adults 21+: up to 2 oz in public, 2 lbs at home. This statute applies to amounts exceeding legal limits or by persons under 21.

statute_title: Controlled Substance Crime in the First Degree
elements: Defendant unlawfully sold one or more mixtures of a total weight of 10 grams or more containing cocaine, heroin, or methamphetamine
OR possessed 25 grams or more of cocaine, heroin, or methamphetamine
mandatory_minimum: Presumptive committed sentence per sentencing guidelines
enhancements: Sale in a school zone, park, or public housing
notes: First-degree is the most serious drug offense. Weight thresholds vary by substance. Sentencing guidelines grid determines presumptive sentence based on severity level and criminal history.

elements: Defendant possessed drug paraphernalia
With knowledge that the paraphernalia was to be used to introduce a controlled substance into the body
notes: Petty misdemeanor — no jail time. Sale or delivery of paraphernalia is a misdemeanor under § 152.093.

offense_class: Misdemeanor; Gross Misdemeanor (if prior conviction or motivated by bias)
elements: Defendant committed an act with intent to cause fear in another of immediate bodily harm or death
OR intentionally inflicted or attempted to inflict bodily harm upon another
enhancements: Prior conviction within two years (gross misdemeanor)
notes: Fifth-degree assault is the lowest-level assault offense in Minnesota. Does not require actual injury.

elements: Defendant assaulted another with a dangerous weapon
The weapon was capable of causing great bodily harm or death
enhancements: Peace officer or other protected victim (10 years)
Substantial or great bodily harm inflicted
notes: Dangerous weapon includes firearms, knives, and other instruments. First-degree assault (§ 609.221) covers great bodily harm — up to 20 years.

offense_class: Misdemeanor (1st offense); Gross Misdemeanor (prior domestic conviction within 10 years); Felony (two or more prior domestic convictions within 10 years)
elements: Defendant committed an assault as defined in § 609.02, subd. 10
Against a family or household member as defined in § 518B.01, subd. 2
mandatory_minimum: Minimum fine of 30% of maximum fine authorized
enhancements: Prior qualified domestic violence-related offense within 10 years (gross misdemeanor)
Two or more prior qualified domestic violence offenses within 10 years (felony)
notes: Qualified domestic violence-related offenses include violations from other states. Court must impose fine of not less than 30% of maximum. Domestic abuse no contact order (DANCO) routinely issued.

elements: Defendant assaulted a family or household member by strangulation
Strangulation means intentionally impeding normal breathing or circulation of the blood by applying pressure on the throat or neck or by blocking the nose or mouth
notes: Standalone felony regardless of prior domestic assault convictions. Enacted to address lethality risk — strangulation is the strongest predictor of domestic homicide.

penalty_min: Life with possibility of release after 30 years
elements: Defendant caused the death of a human being
With premeditation and intent to kill, OR during the commission of certain felonies (criminal sexual conduct, arson, robbery, kidnapping, burglary, drive-by shooting, escape, etc.)
notes: Minnesota does not have the death penalty. First-degree murder carries mandatory life sentence. Possibility of supervised release after 30 years in most cases.

elements: Defendant caused the death of a human being with intent to kill but without premeditation
OR caused the death while committing a felony not listed in first-degree statute
enhancements: Committed while committing a felony (felony murder)
notes: Includes intentional murder without premeditation and unintentional felony murder. Sentencing guidelines severity level 10 (intentional) or 11 (drive-by).

elements: Defendant intentionally caused the death of another in the heat of passion provoked by such words or acts of another as would provoke a person of ordinary self-control
OR violated a restraining order and caused the death
notes: Heat of passion killing — adequate provocation reduces murder to manslaughter.

elements: Defendant caused the death of another by culpable negligence creating an unreasonable risk, and consciously took chances of causing death or great bodily harm
notes: Culpable negligence standard — more than ordinary negligence but less than intent to harm. Commonly charged in negligent gun handling and reckless driving deaths.

elements: Defendant took personal property from the person or in the presence of another
By using or threatening the imminent use of force against any person to overcome resistance or compel acquiescence
notes: Simple robbery — no weapon required, just force or threat of force.

elements: Defendant committed a robbery while armed with a dangerous weapon or article used or fashioned to lead the victim to believe it is a dangerous weapon
OR inflicted bodily harm upon another during the robbery
enhancements: First-degree aggravated robbery (armed with firearm or other dangerous weapon)
notes: First-degree (§ 609.245, subd. 1) involves a dangerous weapon — up to 20 years. Second-degree (subd. 2) involves implied weapon — up to 15 years.

elements: Defendant entered a building without consent
With intent to commit a crime therein
When another person, not an accomplice, was present in the building
AND defendant possessed a weapon or dangerous article, assaulted a person, or used or threatened use of force
notes: First-degree requires occupied dwelling plus additional aggravating factor. Most serious burglary offense.

elements: Defendant entered a dwelling without consent and with intent to commit a crime therein
OR entered a building without consent with a tool, explosive, or weapon
notes: Dwelling burglary without the aggravating factors of first degree.

elements: Defendant entered a building without consent
With intent to commit a crime therein, or committed a crime while in the building
notes: Non-dwelling, non-aggravated burglary. Includes commercial buildings.

penalty_max: 90 days (misdemeanor); 1 year (gross misdemeanor); 5 years ($1,000–$4,999); 10 years ($5,000–$34,999); 20 years ($35,000+)
elements: Defendant intentionally and without claim of right took, used, transferred, concealed, or retained possession of movable property of another
Without the owner's consent and with intent to permanently deprive the owner
enhancements: Theft from a person (felony regardless of amount)
notes: Aggregation of multiple thefts from same victim within 6 months allowed for charging purposes. Includes theft by swindle, embezzlement, and theft of services.

penalty_max: 5 years (1 victim); 10 years (2 victims); 15 years (3+ victims); 20 years ($35,000+ loss)
elements: Defendant used or possessed another person's identity information without consent
With intent to commit, aid, or abet any unlawful activity
notes: Identity information includes name, SSN, date of birth, driver's license number, and financial account numbers.

elements: Defendant obtained property or services by intentional false representation
Which was calculated to deceive and did deceive the victim
With intent to permanently deprive the owner
notes: Theft by swindle is Minnesota's primary fraud statute. Encompasses financial fraud, investment fraud, and consumer fraud.

statute_title: Check Forgery — Offering a Forged Check
offense_class: Felony ($250+); Gross Misdemeanor ($250 or less with 2+ checks); Misdemeanor (single check under $250)
elements: Defendant offered, issued, or delivered a forged check
Knowing the check was forged
With intent to defraud
notes: Includes counterfeited and altered checks. Separate from general forgery statute.

offense_class: Felony (3 years max); Gross Misdemeanor (certain documents)
elements: Defendant falsely made or altered a writing or object with intent to defraud
OR uttered a forged writing or object knowing it to be forged
notes: General forgery statute. Check forgery has separate, more detailed statute at § 609.631.

statute_title: Criminal Sexual Conduct in the First Degree
elements: Defendant engaged in sexual penetration with another person
Under one of the following circumstances: victim was under 13, force or coercion was used, victim was mentally impaired, defendant was in a position of authority, or multiple actors were involved
mandatory_minimum: 144 months (12 years) for offenses involving a victim under 13 or force
enhancements: Repeat sex offender (mandatory life sentence possible under § 609.3455)
notes: Most serious sexual offense. Predatory offender registration required. Mandatory minimum fine of 30% of maximum. Sentencing under sex offender grid.

statute_title: Criminal Sexual Conduct in the Third Degree
elements: Defendant engaged in sexual penetration with another person
Under circumstances such as: victim was 13–15 and defendant was more than 24 months older, force or coercion used, victim was mentally impaired or physically helpless
notes: Involves penetration without the aggravating factors of first degree. Predatory offender registration required.

statute_title: Criminal Sexual Conduct in the Fifth Degree
offense_class: Gross Misdemeanor (first offense); Felony (second or subsequent)
elements: Defendant engaged in nonconsensual sexual contact
OR engaged in masturbation or lewd exhibition in the presence of a minor
notes: Lowest-level criminal sexual conduct charge involving sexual contact, not penetration.

statute_title: Certain Persons Not to Possess Firearms
elements: Defendant possessed a firearm or ammunition
Defendant is a prohibited person: convicted of a crime of violence, convicted of certain drug offenses, subject to a domestic abuse order for protection, or adjudicated mentally ill
mandatory_minimum: 5 years if convicted of a crime of violence and possessing a firearm
enhancements: Prior crime of violence conviction (15 years max)
Possession during commission of another crime
notes: Crime of violence defined at § 624.712, subd. 5. Includes drive-by shooting, murder, robbery, kidnapping, sexual assault, and more.

statute_title: Carrying a Pistol Without a Permit
elements: Defendant carried a pistol in a public place
Without a valid permit to carry
notes: Minnesota is a shall-issue permit state. Permit required for concealed or open carry of a pistol.

elements: Defendant discharged a firearm from a motor vehicle
In a public place, recklessly and without regard for human life
enhancements: Resulting in death (murder in the second degree)
notes: Mandatory consecutive sentence if committed during another felony.

penalty_max: 20 years (general); 40 years (to facilitate felony, sexual assault, or ransom)
elements: Defendant confined or removed another from one place to another without consent
For the purpose of holding victim for ransom, facilitating a felony, committing bodily harm, or terrorizing the victim
notes: Aggravated kidnapping extends maximum to 40 years if purpose was to hold for ransom, facilitate a felony, or cause great bodily harm.

elements: Defendant intentionally set fire to or burned, or aided in burning, any building, structure, or property
Where another person was present at the time
OR the fire resulted in bodily harm to any person
notes: Most serious arson offense — requires occupied building or bodily harm. Treated as crime against the person for sentencing guidelines purposes.

elements: Defendant engaged in brawling or fighting, disturbed a lawful assembly, or engaged in offensive, obscene, or abusive language or boisterous and noisy conduct
Tending reasonably to arouse alarm, anger, or resentment in others
notes: Common public order offense. Often charged alongside other offenses.

offense_class: Misdemeanor; Gross Misdemeanor (certain locations or circumstances)
elements: Defendant intentionally entered or remained on property of another without consent
After being told to leave or after reasonable notice that entry was prohibited
notes: Includes constructive trespass through failure to depart after notice.

statute_title: Fleeing a Peace Officer in a Motor Vehicle
elements: Defendant operated a motor vehicle
Fled or attempted to flee a peace officer by means of speed or other evasive action
After the officer had signaled the defendant to stop by activating lights or siren
enhancements: Death of another person resulting (7 years)
Substantial bodily harm to another (5 years)
notes: Peace officer must have been acting in lawful discharge of duties. Fleeing on foot is a misdemeanor.

elements: Defendant intentionally caused damage to the physical property of another
Without the owner's consent
notes: Damage amount determines severity level. Restitution to victim commonly ordered.

offense_class: Gross Misdemeanor (first offense); Felony (repeat offense or aggravated)
elements: Defendant engaged in a pattern of harassing conduct
The conduct would cause a reasonable person under the circumstances to feel frightened, threatened, oppressed, persecuted, or intimidated
AND did cause this reaction in the victim
notes: Pattern means two or more acts within a five-year period. Includes electronic communication and social media harassment.

statute_title: Violation of an Order for Protection
offense_class: Misdemeanor (first within 10 years); Gross Misdemeanor (second within 10 years); Felony (third or subsequent within 10 years)
elements: A valid order for protection was in effect
Defendant had knowledge of the order
Defendant knowingly violated a provision of the order
enhancements: Prior violations within 10 years escalate classification
notes: Includes domestic abuse no contact orders (DANCO). Violation of DANCO under § 629.75 carries same penalty structure.

elements: Defendant threatened, directly or indirectly, to commit any crime of violence
With purpose to terrorize another or to cause evacuation of a building, public place, or mode of transportation
OR in reckless disregard of the risk of causing such terror
enhancements: Threat involving an explosive or incendiary device
notes: Does not require ability to carry out the threat. Includes threats communicated via electronic means.

statute_title: Obstructing Legal Process, Arrest, or Firefighting
elements: Defendant intentionally obstructed, hindered, or prevented a peace officer, firefighter, or other authorized person
In the lawful execution of their duties
By force or threat of force
notes: Passive resistance (going limp) is generally not sufficient. Requires active physical resistance or interference.

statute_title: Violation of Conditions of Release — Probation Violation
penalty_max: Execution of stayed sentence up to the statutory maximum for the underlying offense
elements: Defendant was placed on probation or conditional release
Defendant violated one or more conditions of that release
Violation was proven by clear and convincing evidence at a hearing
notes: Court may revoke probation and execute the stayed sentence, continue probation with modified conditions, or extend probation. Defendant has right to a Morrissey hearing.

statute_title: Neglect or Endangerment of a Child
offense_class: Gross Misdemeanor (general); Felony (substantial harm or pattern)
elements: Defendant was a parent, legal guardian, or caretaker of a child
Defendant intentionally or negligently caused or permitted the child to be placed in a situation likely to substantially harm the child's physical, mental, or emotional health
notes: Commonly charged alongside DWI when child is in vehicle, or in cases of environmental neglect.

offense_class: Misdemeanor (first); Gross Misdemeanor (second); Felony (third or subsequent)
elements: Defendant hired or offered to hire a person for sexual penetration or sexual contact
enhancements: Patron engaging with minor (felony — up to 20 years)
In a school zone or park
notes: Minnesota law targets buyers (patrons) more heavily than sellers. Victims of sex trafficking may assert affirmative defense under § 609.325.

elements: Defendant intentionally used force, threat of force, intimidation, or deception
To attempt to influence a witness to testify falsely, withhold testimony, or absent themselves from a proceeding
enhancements: Use of force or threats of violence
notes: Includes attempting to influence a witness not to report a crime or cooperate with investigation.

statute_title: Solicitation of Children to Engage in Sexual Conduct
elements: Defendant solicited a child under 16 to engage in sexual conduct
OR communicated with a child under 16 with intent to engage in sexual conduct
enhancements: Use of electronic communication or internet
notes: Includes online enticement. Predatory offender registration required upon conviction.

statute_title: Criminal Vehicular Operation — Substantial Bodily Harm
elements: Defendant operated a motor vehicle in a grossly negligent manner
While under the influence of alcohol or controlled substance
Resulting in substantial bodily harm to another person
enhancements: Great bodily harm (up to 5 years under § 609.2112)
notes: Separate from DWI — focuses on harm caused. Charged in addition to DWI when injuries result.

offense_class: Same as theft based on value of property
penalty_max: 20 years ($35,000+); 10 years ($5,000+); 5 years ($1,000+); 1 year (gross misdemeanor); 90 days (misdemeanor)
elements: Defendant received, possessed, transferred, bought, or concealed stolen property
Knowing or having reason to know the property was stolen
enhancements: Property is a firearm (felony regardless of value)
notes: Same penalty thresholds as theft statute. Knowledge or reason to know property was stolen must be proven.

offense_class: Gross Misdemeanor; Felony (if aggravated or repeat)
elements: Defendant engaged in repeated incidents of intrusive or unwanted acts, words, or gestures
Intended to affect the safety, security, or privacy of another
Regardless of the relationship between the parties
notes: Harassment and stalking are addressed in the same statute. Two incidents constitute a pattern.

statute_title: Failure to Register as Predatory Offender
elements: Defendant was required to register as a predatory offender
Defendant knowingly failed to register, verify information, or provide notice of address change
notes: Mandatory 1-year prison sentence, not subject to early release. Registration required for life or 10 years depending on offense risk level.

elements: Defendant was lawfully held in custody or confinement
Defendant escaped or attempted to escape from custody
enhancements: Escape from a correctional facility (enhanced penalty)
Use of force or weapon during escape
notes: Includes escape from lawful arrest, jail, prison, or court-ordered custody. Sentence runs consecutive to underlying sentence.

elements: Defendant knowingly confined or restrained another person without the person's consent
OR confined or restrained another to facilitate the commission of a felony or to flee after commission
notes: Lesser included offense of kidnapping. Does not require movement of the victim from one place to another.

offense_class: Misdemeanor (first); Gross Misdemeanor (second); Felony (third or subsequent, or if victim under 16)
elements: Defendant willfully and lewdly exposed their body or private parts
In a public place or in the presence of another
In a manner that would be offensive to others
notes: Third or subsequent conviction or exposure to a minor under 16 is a felony. May require sex offender registration.

elements: Defendant intentionally and without claim of right took or drove a motor vehicle without the owner's consent
With intent to permanently deprive the owner
notes: Motor vehicle theft is a felony regardless of the vehicle's value. Joyriding (temporary use) may be charged as unauthorized use of a motor vehicle.

elements: Defendant intentionally took merchandise from a retail store
Without paying for the merchandise
With intent to permanently deprive the store of the property
notes: Charged under the general theft statute. Civil liability to the retailer is separate from criminal penalties.

statute_title: Financial Exploitation of a Vulnerable Adult
elements: Defendant, in a position of trust or with a fiduciary duty to a vulnerable adult
Knowingly obtained or used the vulnerable adult's money, assets, or property
Through undue influence, deception, coercion, harassment, or similar means
notes: Vulnerable adult includes elderly, disabled, and dependent persons. Often charged alongside theft by swindle.

elements: Defendant took a motor vehicle from the person or presence of the owner
By use of force or threat of force
Armed with a dangerous weapon or implying possession of one
enhancements: Bodily harm inflicted during the robbery
notes: Charged under the aggravated robbery statute. Minnesota enacted enhanced carjacking penalties in response to rising incidents.

elements: Defendant manufactured or attempted to manufacture methamphetamine
OR possessed precursor chemicals with intent to manufacture methamphetamine
mandatory_minimum: Presumptive commitment to prison per sentencing guidelines
enhancements: Manufacturing in presence of a child (additional felony)
Resulting in bodily harm to another
notes: Child endangered during meth manufacturing is a separate felony under § 152.137. Environmental cleanup costs may be part of restitution.

elements: Defendant made a false material statement
Under oath or affirmation
In a proceeding before a court, grand jury, or governmental agency
Knowing the statement was false
notes: Materiality of the false statement is an element the state must prove.
